brief_items.problem: Expected "Shubham"; page shows "I build backend systems around problems I actually run into. At Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, I own major parts of the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system: the repository and CI scaffold, the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, and the public detection API. brief_items.question: Enter
brief_items.problem: Expected "The engineering habit I would bring is being explicit about state and about where automation should stop. I built a local Playwright job-application agent in TypeScript and Node, and the design decision that mattered most was making it deterministic and operator-controlled instead of a general autonomous browser agent. Every application moves through an explicit state machine, from DISCOVERED through ELIGIBILITY_CHECK, QUEUED, INSPECT, FILL, READY_TO_SUBMIT, SUBMITTING, and SUBMITTED, rather than being mutated ad hoc. I used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser automation gets dangerous when application state diverges across processes, and every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed environment flags that never default on. I also built a validation ladder, from unit-confirmed up to live-mutation-confirmed, so nothing gets called working just because it passed against a local fixture. Free-text and demographic fields are architecturally blocked from auto-fill and always route to human review. Writing backend services that other teams and players depend on rewards exactly that discipline: clear state transitions, safe defaults, and honesty about what has actually been verified."; page shows "(empty)"
